miners.name: LiveCert — Sourced Answers for Agents
miners.description: Sourced answers for agents and apps across 36 intents, each read live from a named primary source so the caller can check it. Every answer opens with a one-sentence answer, then returns the values as fields, the source and the time it was checked. Compliance: sanctions screening of people, companies and wallets against the OFAC SDN and UN lists with near-match scores; company register records (status, company number, register, registered address and agent, parents) from GLEIF and SEC EDGAR; SEC filings with acceptance times and each 10-Q or 10-K's own XBRL figures; URL reputation from Cloudflare and Quad9 threat DNS and URLhaus, each source named. Research: question answering with every claim cited, web search with dated reports, fact checks with the source URL and evidence sentence, and academic, clinical and news search. Markets: prices and market data for coins, tokens and listed companies, 10-K revenue and earnings, exchange rates and macroeconomic prints (US CPI and unemployment from BLS, the federal funds target range from the New York Fed, euro-area HICP from Eurostat and ECB rates). On-chain: transfer verification with confirmations and the burned base fee, transaction and contract activity across EVM chains, wallet balances, gas, token holders and cross-chain messages. Security: live TLS certificates, URL scans, CVE records and fraud signals. Weather: forecasts, current conditions and storm risk. Also translation, IP geolocation, prediction market outcomes, text extraction, sentiment and classification. Only the question-answering, sentiment and classification sentences are phrased by a model, each with a keyless fallback, and a phrased answer is kept only when every claim cites a numbered source; everything else is computed, not generated.

miners.name: VerifyWire Wash Trading Detection
miners.description: A heuristic read over a token's recent ERC-20 Transfer logs, scanned live over public RPC. It is a signal, not a proof of intent: it measures the patterns wash trading leaves behind. Reciprocal address pairs where value goes out and comes back, self-transfers, plus volume concentrated in a few senders all raise a bounded risk score the answer labels low, elevated or high. The block window is bounded and the node's log range is shrunk when it reports too many results, so a busy token can never exhaust the worker. Reads on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism and Polygon. Answers the WASH_TRADING_DETECTION intent. No API key, nothing cached that can go stale.
